proposal.reactor_type: PFA coil reactor in heated aluminum block (resistive heating replacing microwave)
proposal.residence_time_basis: reactor_volume / total_flow_rate (10 mL / 1.0 mL/min = 10 min), matched directly to batch microwave time
proposal.light_setup: None – thermally driven Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling, no photochemical step

streams.contents: Aromatic bromide (1.0 equiv) + Pd(PPh3)4 or Pd(OAc)2/ligand (5 mol%)
Phenylboronic acid derivative (1.2 equiv) + K2CO3 (2.0 equiv, pre-dissolved, no solids)

proposal.mixer_type: Low-dead-volume PEEK T-mixer (or static mixer chip) upstream of heated coil
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Pd catalyst and aryl bromide are pre-mixed in Stream A to allow oxidative addition complex to begin forming before contacting boronate; combining with Stream B (boronic acid + base) at the T-junction initiates transmetalation only once both reagents are thermally equilibrated, minimizing protodeboronation and premature catalyst decomposition.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas both DMF stock solutions (sparge with N2) to prevent bubble formation and O2-mediated Pd(0) oxidation
0.2 micron in-line filtration of catalyst solution to prevent Pd black/precipitate clogging
Preheat each stream to 50°C via individual preheat loops before the T-mixer to avoid a cold-mixing lag that would extend effective residence time
Confirm full dissolution of K2CO3 (or switch to Cs2CO3/K3PO4 for improved DMF solubility) to avoid solids-induced clogging in 1 mm ID tubing
post_reactor_steps: In-line back-pressure regulator (3 bar) to suppress CO2 outgassing from carbonate base and maintain single liquid phase
Cooling loop (ambient water bath) to quench reaction upon exit from heated zone
Optional in-line liquid-liquid separator to split aqueous base/Pd residues from organic (DMF/product) phase
Pd scavenger cartridge (e.g., SiliaMetS thiol) for catalyst removal
Collection into stirred vessel for standard aqueous workup and isolation
proposal.chemistry_notes: This is a Suzuki-Miyaura biaryl coupling. The microwave batch protocol (50 W, 50°C, 10 min) is translated directly to a thermally heated flow coil with matched residence time and temperature, assuming the microwave dielectric heating simply achieved rapid, uniform bulk heating to 50°C rather than a unique non-thermal effect. Flow allows precise temperature/residence control and eliminates the need for microwave-specific vessels.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Directly matched to the 10 min batch microwave irradiation time, assuming equivalent thermal exposure gives equivalent conversion.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Total 1.0 mL/min (0.5 + 0.5 from two streams) chosen to give a practical 10 mL reactor volume at 10 min residence, compatible with standard flow pumps.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Matched to batch microwave temperature (50°C); assumed the microwave was primarily used for fast, uniform heating rather than specific activation.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Post-mix ArBr concentration estimated at 0.2 M assuming a modest overall reaction volume in the original batch vial (~8 mL for 1.6 mmol); not explicitly stated in protocol, so treated as an assumption.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Low pressure (3 bar) applied mainly to prevent CO2 microbubble formation from carbonate base and maintain stable single-phase flow, not to raise the boiling point (DMF bp 153°C >> 50°C reaction temp).
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: PFA coil in heated block chosen for corrosion resistance to DMF/base and ease of temperature control, replacing microwave cavity heating.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID balances reasonable flow velocity/mixing efficiency with manageable pressure drop and resistance to particulate clogging.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 10 mL calculated from target residence time (10 min) times total flow rate (1.0 mL/min).
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: T-mixer selected for simplicity and low dead volume; adequate given both streams are already homogeneous solutions.

proposal.literature_analogies: Analogous to reported flow Suzuki-Miyaura couplings (e.g., Noël and coworkers, Org. Process Res. Dev.) using Pd(PPh3)4 or Pd(OAc)2, K2CO3/Cs2CO3 base, DMF or DMF/H2O solvent systems in PFA coil reactors at 50–100°C with residence times of 5–15 min, achieving yields comparable to microwave batch conditions (85–95%).
safety_flags: DMF is a reproductive toxicant and skin-absorbable solvent; use closed system with fume hood ventilation and appropriate PPE
Pd catalyst and boronic acid dusts are respiratory irritants; handle stock solution preparation in a fume hood
Carbonate base can release CO2 under heating; ensure BPR is rated and monitored to prevent pressure spikes or seal failure
PFA tubing max rated temperature (~150-200°C) is well above operating temp (50°C), providing safety margin
Regular inspection for Pd black precipitation/clogging in narrow-bore tubing
Aqueous/organic biphasic separator step involves flammable DMF; ensure no open flame near separation equipment
